why: The one review of ticket 1161 in today's CI (scheduled.yaml's hand start takes scope and law). Send back to the tests step, which owns every .github/ file here, 1 blocking class: SC21's read check (.github/ci/workflow-lint/scheduled.ts:184) and its law S9 (.github/ci/workflow-lint/scheduled.test.ts:1458) miss GitHub's other ways to read the whole event: toJSON(github['event']), toJSON(github.event.*) and toJSON(github.*) each pass every lint rule in 27 places, the tests job's step env among them, and dropping the rule's case-insensitive flag leaves all 302 tests green. No path to narrow main was found: SC15, SC11, SC7 and SC6 pin the if, depth, commands and matrix. The branch also conflicts with origin/main 279f97ee0 (pull request 1618) in proof.ts, proof.test.ts, scheduled.yaml and TERMS.md, and that commit makes PROJECTS three, so the new 'four projects' wording goes stale. proof.ts holds: a bad SCOPE or LAW throws in the select step, scheduled.mjs reads the failed select as red, and a valid full ask gives the full set with its law in the record. loosening.sh: 5 unrecognized-change hits on the whole diff and on b163a3792, all stricter or additive; 0 on a22173522.
note: Read-only apart from this row. Container Node 22.23.5, CI=1, nice 19, one worker. Plants were run in a scratch copy outside the repo (tar of the worktree with node_modules linked) and restored: askOf without isLaw red (P8, P9); summary hand line keyed off no triggers red (P11); inProjects without next-visual red (P10); SC21 without the i flag green (302 passed); SC21 law description check dropped green (302 passed); SC21 law default any text red (S8). Read forms were run against lintScheduled by a scratch node script. Not run: D1, which is the lead's dispatch; pnpm typecheck (review rule); scheduled.integration.test.ts. Four finding rows: SC17 accepts SCOPE as the plain text inputs.scope; no law reaches SC21's law description check; the new property laws use raw fc.assert with a hand seed against 0579; the PR has no New names section, and Ask/asked reuse the glossary's ask.
